post.caption: Scientists made diamond rain from plastic. In 2017, a team used a laser on a sheet of polystyrene. The laser sent two shock waves through the plastic, and X ray flashes caught the diamonds as they formed. Nearly every carbon atom in the plastic turned into a tiny diamond. Scientists believe the same thing happens about 10,000 kilometers down inside Neptune, where diamonds may sink for thousands of years and could grow to millions of carats. The diamonds made in the lab lasted only nanoseconds.
